subsections.subsection_title: Patient asks: "Does this mean my baby has Down syndrome?"

blocks.text: "No. This result does not diagnose Down syndrome. It means that, based on the factors included in the screening test, the chance is higher than expected. We would need diagnostic testing to confirm or exclude the diagnosis."

subsections.subsection_title: Patient asks: "Why do I need another test?"

blocks.text: "Because screening estimates risk, whereas diagnostic testing can determine much more definitively whether the fetus has a particular chromosomal abnormality."

subsections.subsection_title: Patient asks: "Can you guarantee that my baby is normal if the screening is low risk?"

blocks.text: "No screening test can guarantee that a baby has no medical or chromosomal condition. A low-risk result significantly reduces the chance of the conditions screened for, but it does not eliminate all risk."

"Counsel this 12-week pregnant woman about first-trimester screening."

blocks.text: "I would first introduce myself, confirm her identity, ensure privacy and establish what she already understands about prenatal screening."
"I would explain that first-trimester screening estimates the chance of certain chromosomal conditions, particularly trisomy 21, trisomy 18 and trisomy 13."

"Depending on the screening pathway, this may involve an ultrasound assessment including nuchal translucency together with maternal blood tests such as PAPP-A and free β-hCG. Cell-free DNA or NIPT is another highly accurate screening option for common trisomies."
"I would emphasise that these are screening tests and not diagnostic tests. A high-risk result does not mean that the fetus definitely has the condition."

"If screening indicates an increased chance, I would arrange appropriate specialist counselling and discuss further options, which may include additional screening or diagnostic testing such as chorionic villus sampling or amniocentesis."
"I would also explain that screening does not replace the routine detailed anomaly ultrasound because chromosomal screening cannot exclude all structural abnormalities."
"I would provide balanced, non-directive information, answer her questions and support her in making a decision that is appropriate for her."
